title: Germany – Installation of doors and windows and related components – TIS II - Innentüren, Zargen, Holztüren
description: Die Behörde für Justiz und Verbraucherschutz beabsichtigt, eine für den Justizvollzug nicht mehr benötigte Teilfläche des aktuellen Geländes der JVA Fuhlsbüttel freizuziehen. Zu diesem Zwecke ist geplant, die sich auf der Teilfläche befindlichen Nutzungseinheiten der Anstalt durch die Realisierung zweier Neubauten auf die weiterhin genutzte Fläche zu verlagern. Die aktuelle Versorgungsstruktur der JVA Fuhlsbüttel sowie die Wegeführungen auf dem Anstaltsgelände sind aufgrund des Freizugs der Teilfläche anzupassen. Zur Abgrenzung der verbleibenden Anstaltsfläche gegenüber der freizuziehenden Teilfläche ist außerdem die Außensicherung der JVA Fuhlsbüttel in Teilen neu zu planen und zu versetzen. Hierfür sind einige Bestandsbauten der Anstalt vollständig oder in Teilen zurückzubauen Am Standort der JVA Fuhlsbüttel sollen zwei Ersatzneubauten erstellt werden; ein Ausbildungsgebäude (A), dieses zentral auf dem JVA-Gelände, sowie ein Garagen- und Verwaltungsgebäude (B) mit Anbindung an eine Bestandspforte. Die jeweils viergeschossigen Neubauten werden als Mischkonstruktion aus Mauerwerk, Ortbeton und Betonfertigteilelementen, ohne Unterkellerung mit einer Sohle aus WU-Beton erstellt. Die Außenhüllen der Gebäude werden mit Verblendsteinen bekleidet und erhalten ein Satteldach als Pfettendach aus Nadelholz mit Metalldacheindeckung. Sämtliche Fensteröffnungen werden vergittert, Hauptgegenstand der Ausschreibung sind die Lieferung und Montage von Innentüren aus Holz- und Holzwerkstoffen einschl. Stahlzargen. _________________________________________________________________________ Wesentliche Arbeiten: Für die Neubauten ATV DIN 18355 Tischlerarbeiten

title: Germany – Contractor's all-risk insurance services – BauRisk-Versicherung
description: degewo AG ist mit 82.000 eigen- und fremdverwalteten Wohnungen eines der größten kommunalen Wohnungsunternehmen in Deutschland mit Sitz in Berlin. Die Immobilienbestände befinden sich in allen Stadtteilen Berlins und vergrößern sich im Zuge von Investitionsmaßnahmen stetig. Die netzWerk ist als 100%ige Tochtergesellschaft der degewo im Bereich Energieversorgung und technische Gebäudeinfrastruktur als konzernangehöriges Dienstleistungsunternehmen tätig. Der netzWerk obliegt dabei unter anderem die effiziente, klimaschonende und intelligente Versorgung des Konzerngebäudebestandes mit Wärme und Strom. Gegenstand ist eine kombinierte Bauleistungs- und Haftpflicht-Versicherung (BauRisk-Versicherung) mit den Vertragsteilen Bauleistungs-, Betriebshaftpflicht- (einschließlich Bauherren-, Umwelthaftpflicht- und Umweltschaden-) und Berufshaftpflicht-Versicherung für alle Bau- und Montageprojekte (Strom-/Wärmeerzeugungsanlagen und Strom-/Wärmeversorgungsanlagen einschließlich Photovoltaikanlagen sowie Kabel- und Glasfasernetze) der Versicherungsnehmerin mit einer Gesamt-Bausumme von über 200.000 € bis 25.000.000 € und einem Planungsbeginn ab 2027 einschließlich der dazugehörigen Tiefbaumaßnahmen mit einer jeweiligen vorläufigen Gesamtbausumme über 200.000 € und bis 25.000.000 € innerhalb der Bundesrepublik Deutschland, die von der Versicherungsnehmerin oder den versicherten Unternehmen (gem. Ziffer 2a) beauftragt und während der Vertragslaufzeit begonnen werden. Sämtliche am Bau beteiligten Firmen der Bereiche Ausführung und Planung sollen im Rahmen dieser kombinierten Bauleistungs-, Montage- und Haftpflicht-Versicherung abgesichert werden und müssen insofern keine eigene Versicherung mehr vorhalten. Als Versicherungsort gelten für jedes Bauprojekt das gesamte Baustellengelände inkl. für das Projekt genutzte Lagergelegenheiten bzw. Verbindungswege zwischen den vorgenannten Orten innerhalb der Bundesrepublik Deutschland. Im Ergebnis des Vergabeverfahrens kann ein Versichererkonsortium nach den zum Gegenstand dieses Verfahrens gemachten Vergabeunterlagen gebildet werden. Für ein Führungsangebot wird eine Zeichnungsquote von mindestens 40 % vorausgesetzt werden, für ein Beteiligungsangebot eine Zeichnungsquote von mindestens 20 %. Die Bewerber erklären mit der Angebotsabgabe die grundsätzliche Bereitschaft, mit den von der Auftraggeberin ausgewählten Mitgliedern des Versichererkonsortiums zusammenzuarbeiten.

buyer: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control
title: Sweden – Health services – SPR/260834 - Provision of genomic epidemiology and public health bioinformatics training
description: The overall objective of this tender is to procure a Framework Contract to strengthen the capacity for genomic epidemiology and public health bioinformatics through interdisciplinary trainings, which is crucial for response during a pandemic or unexpected major public health events. The general objectives of the trainings are to support countries in building up their capacity in genomic epidemiology and bioinformatics for public health purposes, and to increase the interdisciplinary collaboration between bioinformaticians, epidemiologists and microbiologists within a country to facilitate the routine use of genomic information for surveillance, preparedness, and outbreak response. Activities shall also enhance data sharing and collaborations between public health institutions and ECDC, and enhanced networking activities will foster cross-border collaborations. The target groups for the trainings are professionals working in public health institutions with a background in computational biology and bioinformatics; and professionals working in public health institutions who do not have a specific background in bioinformatics. The aims of the trainings are: * To allow the professionals with a background in computational biology and bioinformatics to: - enhance and extend their skills in order to strengthen their capacity in the field of public health bioinformatics; - better understand the needs and concepts of epidemiology and public health microbiology, with a focus on the inputs and outputs needed by their counterparts (i.e. microbiologists, epidemiologists, professionals in public health surveillance and response) to take rapid and informed public health action. * To allow the professionals without a background in computational biology/bioinformatics to: - gain a better understanding of how genomic epidemiology can be applied in a public health context with special focus on how traditional and genomic data can be jointly analysed, interpreted and used for public health purposes; - become more familiar with the concepts, formats and conventions commonly used in microbial genomics, and get a better understanding of how the structure and format of the data can be used to streamline the data analysis process; - better understand the concepts behind and use of the most common bioinformatic tools and pipelines used for epidemiological analyses, including limitations and possible alternatives; and - gain a better overview of the basic principles, options for and best practices of data storage, management and sharing, with a specific focus on sequencing data and associated metadata.

title: Germany – Architectural services for outdoor areas – Neubau Bildungscampus Eslohe - Objektplanung Freianlagen
description: Am Bildungsstandort Eslohe befindet sich das zentrale Kompetenzzentrum des Dachdeckerhandwerks in Westfalen. Der Standort vereint die schulische Berufsausbildung, die Unterbringung der Auszubildenden, Verpflegungsangebote sowie Maßnahmen der Aus- und Weiterbildung in einem zusammenhängenden Campus. Die bestehende Gebäudeinfrastruktur stammt überwiegend aus den Jahren 1968 und 1985. Die vorhandenen Gebäude entsprechen sowohl hinsichtlich ihrer funktionalen Struktur als auch in Bezug auf die bauliche, energetische und nutzungsspezifische Qualität nicht mehr den heutigen Anforderungen an einen modernen Bildungs- und Internatsstandort. Insbesondere die bestehende Mischnutzung von Unterricht, Verwaltung, Wohnen und Verpflegung innerhalb der vorhandenen Gebäude führt zu organisatorischen Einschränkungen und erschwert eine zeitgemäße Umsetzung des Bildungsauftrags. Auch die Unterbringungssituation im Wohnheimbereich entspricht nicht mehr den aktuellen Anforderungen. Die derzeit überwiegend vorhandenen Mehrbettzimmer mit Gemeinschaftssanitäranlagen bieten nur eingeschränkte Aufenthalts- und Wohnqualität. Darüber hinaus bestehen Defizite bei den Freizeit-, Aufenthalts- und Kommunikationsflächen für die Auszubildenden. Im Rahmen einer Machbarkeitsstudie wurden verschiedene Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten für den Standort untersucht. Auf Grundlage der Ergebnisse hat sich der Auftraggeber für die Realisierung eines Ersatzneubaukonzeptes entschieden. Damit sollen die funktionalen, organisatorischen, pädagogischen und energetischen Anforderungen langfristig erfüllt und gleichzeitig der laufende Schul- und Wohnheimbetrieb während der Realisierung sichergestellt werden.

Für die im Baufeld befindlichen Bestandsbäume wurde bereits eine Fällgenehmigung eingereicht. Sollte die Asphaltdeckschicht aufgrund der Witterungsverhältnisse erst verspätet ausgeführt werden können, ist dies zulässig. Der betroffene Bereich darf jedoch auch abschnittsweise nicht länger als 7 Wochen gesperrt werden. Daher muss zumindest die Asphalttragschicht eingebaut werden, bevor es zu einer längeren Unterbrechung kommt bzw. um sicherzustellen, dass der Parkplatz nicht länger als 7 Wochen gesperrt bleibt.

buyer: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
title: Germany – Vocational training services – 10018858-Implementation of TVET support and women's economic empowerment activities in Sierra Leone
description: Sierra Leone faces persistent poverty, high informality and limited job creation, disproportionately affecting women and youth. Agriculture is the largest employer, yet value chains are fragmented, processing is weak, and access to finance, quality infrastructure and certification is limited. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system suffers from outdated curricula, insufficient equipment and low private sector engagement, constraining labour market relevance, especially for women and returnees. The "Youth Employment Promotion through Socio Ecological and Economic Transformation of selected rural Value Chains" (EET project), commissioned by BMZ with EU co funding, supports inclusive, market oriented growth and better employment along selected value chains (cassava, coffee/cocoa, vegetables, poultry). It strengthens micro, small and medium sized enterprises (MSMEs) and the enabling ecosystem, with a strong focus on Women's Economic Empowerment (WEE) and youth integration. The project applies a concise multi level approach: support MSMEs with training, coaching and finance to improve productivity and market access; strengthen ecosystem actors (finance, certification, cooperatives, processing centres) to enhance services and linkages; and upgrade TVET through demand driven Competence Based Education and Training (CBET) curricula, improved facilities at Government Technical Institutes (GTIs) in Kabala, Kailahun, Koidu and Mattru Jong, teacher capacity building and institutionalised private sector engagement for apprenticeships and certification via Industry Sector Advisory Committees. WEE is embedded throughout. The project strengthens six representative bodies advancing women's economic rights (e.g. Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment - GEWE - Act), introduces gender transformative modules (Gender makes Business Sense - GmBS; Gender Action Learning Systems - GALS; Gender Model Family - GMF) via public and private providers, and delivers mentoring and awareness campaigns to address norms and improve women"s access to resources, markets and decision making. Outcomes are tracked with recognised tools such as the (pro )Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (pro WEAI). Key results targeted include: - Improved competitiveness of MSMEs with measurable employment effects for women and youth. - Upgraded GTIs and at least nine demand oriented, gender responsive curricula operational; teachers trained in learner centred CBET; trainees certified in line with National Council for Technical and Vocational Education (NCTVE) standards in the initial phase. - Stronger institutional conditions for women's economic participation, including operational representative bodies, integrated gender transformative modules, and functioning mentoring and communication platforms. - Enhanced market access through strengthened outgrower networks, cooperative services and business linkages, enabling more equitable participation of women and young producers. The approach is rights based, conflict and context sensitive, and climate aware. It promotes green and circular economy elements in training and enterprise support, limits environmental footprints and applies Do No Harm principles. Implementation aligns with national policies (TVET Policy, Dual Apprenticeship Policy) under the coordination of the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development, with the Ministry of Technical and Higher Education (MTHE) and NCTVE responsible for TVET standards and certification, and the Ministry of Gender and Children's Affairs and civil society partners advancing WEE. Continuous monitoring, learning and adaptive management ensure data driven steering and accountability to BMZ and the EU. EU visibility will follow EU visual identity guidelines; co branding with BMZ/GIZ will follow donor rules.?

description: The GIZ programme "UfM Hub for Jobs, Trade and Investment II", commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and co-financed by the European Union, strengthens regional economic cooperation and policy dialogue across the Mediterranean, reinforcing the Union for the Mediterranean (UfM) as the principal regional platform for cooperation between European and Southern Mediterranean partner countries. The programme contributes to the implementation of the EU Pact for the Mediterranean and supports the regional Team Europe Initiative (TEI) "Jobs through Trade & Investment in the Southern Neighbourhood", promoting structured exchange among governments, regional organisations, the private sector, financial institutions and other stakeholders. While the programme focuses on UfM Member States in North Africa and the Middle East, EU Member States and the Western Balkans are actively involved in peer learning and the exchange of best practices. A further priority is strengthening the institutional capacities of the UfM Secretariat to enhance its role in facilitating regional cooperation. Within this framework, the programme also implements the regional Action "Digital Transformation in the Southern Neighbourhood" (DTSN), which covers the thematic areas Digital and Telecommunications Regulation, Cybersecurity (implemented by the GIZ Global Program "Partnerships for Cybersecurity"), and Digital Skills. DTSN supports countries in advancing regulatory approximation with EU best practice, strengthening national regulatory authorities (NRAs), institutionalising the Euro-Mediterranean Regulators Group (EMERG), improving national cybersecurity governance, and developing regional digital skills systems geared to the needs of MSMEs and business support organisations.

description: The objective of GIZ's global project Sustainable Economic Transformation and Sustainable Finance is to advance the transformation towards a more sustainable economy and financial sector, grounded in international standards and global agendas. To this end, the project implements activities in three main areas of intervention: - Pillar 1: Fostering global knowledge exchange and peer-learning regarding the sustainable transformation of the economy and the financial sector. - Pillar 2: Supporting development of policy and regulatory frameworks in partner countries governing the transformation toward a sustainable economy and financial sector in partner countries. - Pillar 3: Providing advisory services and technical assistance to embed sustainability in governance and financial decision-making of financial institutions. In pillar 2, the project supports partner countries in aligning their financial regulatory and policy frameworks with international standards and best practices on sustainable finance. This encompasses, for example, the development of taxonomies, disclosure regulations, sustainable financial product standards or policies on ESG risk management. The project's activities include, for example, supporting the development of national taxonomies in Rwanda, Peru, Senegal, Ghana, The Philippines, and Mexico. The support provided by GIZ is comprehensive, including strategic advice, capacity building, design of multi-stakeholder processes (e.g., coordination of technical expert groups, support for public consultation), drafting advice (e.g., on the selection of sectors and screening criteria), and supporting the taxonomy's dissemination and implementation. This process is complemented by peer-learning opportunities and featuring lessons learned from implementation in partner countries in relevant international and regional forums. The objective of this tender is to establish a flexible pool of specialized technical expertise that can support sustainable finance taxonomy initiatives in partner countries designated by GIZ during the contract period. The contractor will provide advisory services covering the development, enhancement and implementation of sustainable finance taxonomies, as well as related analytical work, capacity building and knowledge products.

title: GOCO Industry Day
description: Executive Summary The current operating strategy for Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) Army ammunition plants requires reassessment to ensure the Organic Industrial Base can meet future requirements for safety, responsiveness, capacity, modernization, supply-chain resilience, and affordable lifecycle performance. Traditional GOCO competition and contract approaches may not consistently create the incentives, flexibility, or accountability necessary to operate Government-owned facilities as modern and competitive manufacturing enterprises. In particular, existing approaches may overemphasize Government-directed workload and reimbursed facility operations rather than operator responsibility for productive utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce development, workload capture, and operational performance. The Government is seeking industry input on a commercially disciplined GOCO operating model that preserves Government mission priorities while providing the operating contractor meaningful responsibility and flexibility to manage the facility as a competitive manufacturing enterprise. Under such a model, the contractor would be expected to sustain, modernize, maintain, and improve the facility through efficient operations, productive utilization, pursuit of approved workload, and sound business practices. The Government seeks to identify contracting, workload, risk-allocation, facility-use, oversight, intellectual-property, and performance-management constructs that will enable this model while preserving appropriate Government accountability, safety, security, and access to required production capacity. Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE AS&A) is assessing the future GOCO operating strategy before proceeding with future GOCO competitions. Purpose Army Contracting Command � Rock Island, on behalf of PAE AS&A, intends to host an Industry Day in November 2026 focused on transforming the operating strategy for GOCO Army ammunition plants. Specific Industry Day details will be provided separately; registration is not currently required. This Request for Information (RFI), together with the subsequent Industry Day, will help the Government understand feasible business and operating models for future GOCO facilities. The Government will use industry feedback to inform discussion of alternative approaches to facility operations, modernization, workload management, contract structure, and oversight. Objective The Government�s objective is to establish a commercially disciplined operating model for GOCO Army ammunition plants that improves responsiveness to Warfighter requirements while sustaining long-term plant viability, modernization, competitiveness, and accountability. The desired model would provide the operating contractor with appropriate flexibility and meaningful responsibility to manage facility utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce, supply chain, and approved workload. The Government seeks input on the risk-allocation mechanisms, workload authorities, facility-use structures, performance measures, and oversight approaches necessary to support this model while preserving Government mission priorities. The desired end state is a modern, flexible production enterprise capable of efficiently increasing, reducing, pausing, restarting, changing over, and surging production in response to Warfighter need without disproportionate impacts to cost, schedule, quality, workforce readiness, safety, or production capability. The Government is particularly interested in performance measures that demonstrate: Safe and reliable operations; Schedule reliability and order-to-delivery responsiveness; Plant availability and production throughput; Rapid changeover, shutdown, restart, and surge capability; Flexible, modular, dual-use, and/or automated manufacturing capacity; Effective maintenance, workforce, and supply-chain management; Competitive lifecycle cost and productive utilization; Modernization outcomes that improve operating performance; and Appropriate transparency and accountability without unnecessary Government direction of day-to-day operations. Areas of Consideration The Government developed the attached questionnaire based on the following interconnected areas of consideration. Respondents are requested to complete the associated questionnaire and provide practical recommendations, examples, and lessons learned from relevant commercial, defense-industrial, or other manufacturing environments. The Government is particularly interested in responses that: Describe a complete and coherent commercial operating model rather than isolated contractual changes; Identify recommended Government and contractor responsibilities; Explain the proposed allocation of risk and opportunity; Identify measurable outcomes and recommended key performance indicators; Describe the conditions necessary to modernize facilities and maintain flexible production capacity; Address how the model would operate during high-demand, low-demand, shutdown, restart, and surge conditions; Identify legal, regulatory, technical, security, safety, qualification, or business constraints requiring further Government consideration; and Contain data that supports its recommended solutions. 1. Commercial Operating Model and Risk Allocation The Government seeks input on operating models in which the contractor manages a Government-owned facility with commercial discipline while meeting Government mission priorities. Topics may include: Operator responsibilities, decision rights, and accountability; Allocation of demand, utilization, revenue, operating-cost, maintenance, modernization, obsolescence, and performance risk; Contractor responsibility for productive utilization and continuous improvement; Mechanisms that encourage modernization as an operating outcome rather than a discrete facility-improvement project; Gain-sharing, profit-sharing, retained earnings, or reinvestment approaches; Treatment of contractor-funded improvements at contract transition; and Protection of Government interests while maintaining meaningful contractor performance and market risk. 2. Demand, Capacity, and Workload Management The Government seeks input on how Government requirements and approved non-Government workload can be integrated to improve plant utilization, responsiveness, and long-term viability. Topics may include: Government demand forecasting and demand-signal quality; Government mission-priority requirements; Capacity reservation, surge, turn-down, shutdown, restart, and reconstitution; Minimum Government commitments, if necessary, and the appropriate purpose and scope of such commitments; Integration of Government, commercial, Foreign Military Sales, and other approved workload; Multi-year procurement and workload-planning approaches; Workforce retention and readiness during periods of variable demand; and Mechanisms for balancing Government access to capacity with contractor responsibility for utilization. 3. Modern, Flexible, and Resilient Production The Government seeks concepts for modernizing GOCO production capability to improve agility, resilience, and efficient response to changing demand. Topics may include: Flexible, modular, dual-use, and automated production lines; Rapid product changeover and qualification; Planned shutdown, restart, and surge capability; Automation, robotics, digital manufacturing, digital twins, and predictive maintenance; Equipment replacement, facility renewal, and obsolescence management; Workforce cross-training and critical-skill retention; Supply-chain resilience and access to existing U.S. industrial capacity; and Technical, regulatory, contractual, qualification, or facility barriers that limit modernization and flexibility. 4. Commercial Workload and Market Access The Government seeks feedback on conditions that would enable the operating contractor to pursue and execute eligible non-Government wor

title: Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) Spacecraft Support
description: This is a Sources Sought notice for market research purposes only. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). The U.S. Government is seeking to identify qualified sources capable of providing sustaining engineering, operational support, and eventual decommissioning for the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) spacecraft fleet. The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of the capabilities, capacity, and qualifications of potential contractors to support the spacecraft bus and associated subsystems of the DMSP constellation. DMSP is the longest-running production satellite program, providing critical weather and environmental data for military operations. Operations are managed jointly by the U.S. Space Force and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). title: Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) Call for Whitepapers for Mission Development Zone (MDZ) Outgrant
description: ** The response due date has been extended from 2 October 2026 to 16 October 2026** 1. DESCRIPTION 1.1. Growth of the U.S. Domestic Space industry has resulted in a greater demand for use of real property at U.S. Space Force (USSF) Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30), Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) by private and commercial entities to conduct spaceport support, payload processing, hardware manufacturing, testing, logistics, and other space-related activities. Ensuring that United States operators can efficiently process space systems, conduct missions in space, launch, and reenter United States airspace is critical to economic growth, national security, and accomplishing Federal space objectives. 1.2. SLD 30 requests white paper responses from United States Commercial Providers as defined by 51 U.S.C. � 50101(7) engaged in space transportation, spaceport support, spacecraft manufacturing, payload processing, assembly, test, space logistics, or other space-related operations on the buildout of the Mission Development Zone (MDZ). Respondents will offer insights, perspectives, and approaches to obtain real property-use agreements to finance, design, construct, operate, and maintain spaceport infrastructure. Industry insights from whitepaper submissions may be utilized to drive future RFI / RFP announcements issued by SLD 30. Specifically, the MDZ infrastructure is intended to provide critical support services to the Department of War (DoW), commercial spaceflight, and other spaceport users at an undeveloped area located in the southern region of VSFB�s North Base area. Development and utilization of the MDZ will be in support of maximizing spaceport capability and assured access to space to achieve national security objectives. 1.3. Description of Premises is at Exhibit B. Please note that the MDZ is not a space launch complex (launch pad), but rather a flexible development zone dedicated to supporting the broader spaceport ecosystem. This includes, but is not limited to, payload processing, hazardous processing, spaceport logistics, commodity storage, launch and mission control, research and development, spacecraft integration, and administrative/engineering spaces. 1.4. The USSF is gathering market intelligence to determine the feasibility of a future real property outgrant under 10 U.S.C. � 2667 to a commercial space services provider, spaceport support provider, launch service provider (LSP), space infrastructure provider, or other space-related entity to construct spaceport-related support infrastructure. MDZ support infrastructure may include, but is not limited to, the following activities: processing, manufacturing, logistics, and administrative support activities. Data gathered from white paper responses will directly inform the Government in determining optimal MDZ utilization and potential infrastructure requirements to meet Government and industry launch requirements. 1.5. To support its ongoing spaceport capacity expansion, Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30) continuously evaluates opportunities and fields requests for new missions. Accordingly, SLD 30 provides discretionary site access and information to prospective partners at any time. Spaceport users and providers responding to this call for whitepapers wishing to view the site may request a property viewing. Please note that scheduling a site visit does not constitute grounds for extending the submittal deadline. 2. CONDITIONS 2.1. This call for whitepapers is not governed by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and is not a Request for Information (RFI), a Request for Proposal (RFP), a Request for Quote (RFQ), nor a solicitation announcement. Content of whitepapers will provide industry insight to assist the Government in scoping, planning, and defining requirements for the proposed MDZ. Content of the whitepapers may assist the Government in generating future contract requirements. Submitters agree and allow the USSF to use the information in the submissions for this purpose. 2.2. This call for whitepapers is issued solely for informational and planning purposes, and the Government is under no obligation to allocate property. The information contained herein is current as of the publication date but subject to change; it is not binding and may be amended in the future. While SLD 30 intends to review submissions, it is under no obligation to do so and reserves the right to cancel or amend the call for whitepapers at its sole discretion. 2.3. No funds are available to fund the whitepaper requested and the Government will not pay or reimburse any costs associated with responding to this request. 2.4. Any future facility where energetic propellants, hazardous materials, and/or ordnance will be used, processed, or stored will require the development of an explosives site plan. To assist the Government in layout and zoning analysis, respondents should outline any anticipated explosive safety arcs, quantity-distance (QD) requirements, or specialized hazard mitigation constraints. 3. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS To assist the U.S. Space Force in scoping and planning for the Mission Development Zone (MDZ), respondents are requested to provide a whitepaper that addresses the following areas. The goal is to gather information on industry needs, operational concepts, and technical requirements to shape the future development of the MDZ. 3.1. Spaceport, Support, and Related Infrastructure Capability. To meet future U.S. Government and commercial space requirements, the USSF seeks to establish robust spaceport support and related infrastructure at VSFB. The MDZ, positioned in the southern area of North VSFB, has been assessed as a potentially viable location for development of infrastructure required for the preparation, operation, and support of launch programs, spacecraft assembly, payload processing, space logistics, and other supporting commercial or industrial activities that enable the spaceport ecosystem. The Government is seeking insights from industry regarding the MDZ layout and planned utilization including types of facilities that would be most beneficial to launch providers in this location. Respondents should provide an assessment with respect to the compatibility of the property with proposed concept of operations. To assist the Government in understanding this capability, respondents should provide a list of all desired facility developments intended to be constructed at the MDZ. 3.2. Payload Processing and Hardware Requirements. A primary objective of the MDZ development is to address current installation capacity constraints regarding payload processing. If a respondent�s concept of operations involves payload or hardware processing, the Government requests specific information regarding requirements to process modern 5-meter-class payloads and next-generation fairings. Respondents should describe necessary facility specifications to include cleanroom class ratings (e.g., ISO 7, ISO 8), overhead crane hook heights, clear span ceiling heights, and projected annual processing throughput. (Note: If a respondent�s proposed operations do not involve payload processing, this section may be omitted). 3.3. Benefit to the Spaceport Ecosystem. Respondents should describe how their proposed operations, facilities, or infrastructure developments will benefit the broader VSFB spaceport ecosystem, the commercial space industry, and U.S. Space Force national security objectives. 3.4. Parcel Selection, Layout Preferences, & Utility Requirements. The MDZ contains roughly 2,100 acres divided into general parcel sizes. The MDZ is located within 5 miles of Vandenberg Airfield with some parcels in the aircraft arrival corridor which will limit building height. title: Portable Special-Purpose High-Purity Nitrogen Generation Systems
description: 1. DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICES This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research, planning, and information purposes in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 10.002, FAR Part 12 (as updated under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul [RFO] model class deviation and E.O. 14275), FAR 15.201(e), and FAR 52.215-3 (Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes). No Solicitation Exists: This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), an Invitation for Bids (IFB), a Request for Quotations (RFQ), or a promise to issue any solicitation in the future. No Commitment: Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The issuance of this RFI does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any product or service whatsoever, nor does it guarantee that a formal procurement will result. Commerciality & RFO Part 12 Application: Market research obtained via this notice will assist the Contracting Officer in determining whether commercial procedures under rewritten FAR Part 12 apply and whether contemplated items meet the statutory definition of a "Commercial Product" or "Commercial Product with Modifications" pursuant to 10 U.S.C. �� 3451�3453 and FAR 2.101. No Reimbursement: The Government will not pay for any information, administrative costs, travel, or submissions incurred in responding to this RFI. All submitted materials shall become Government property and will not be returned. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not be held liable for any use or disclosure of data provided in response to this notice unless clearly marked with proprietary rights legends. 2. PURPOSE & OBJECTIVES Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF), under contracting activity N4523A, is conducting market research to: Assess Commercial & Modified COTS Availability: Determine whether commercial products currently available in the commercial marketplace�or commercial products that can be modified of a type customarily available in the commercial marketplace to meet the Government's requirement�satisfy PSNS & IMF's operational parameters pursuant to RFO FAR Part 12. Evaluate Customary Commercial Practices & Customary Modifications: In accordance with RFO FAR Subpart 12.1 (Pre-solicitation), identify commercial practices regarding warranties, maintenance intervals, testing, and delivery terms, and understand the degree of adaptation required to configure commercial industrial nitrogen plants into shipyard-ready, containerized units. Obtain Specification Feedback: Solicit industry input, risk assessments, and recommendations regarding the Government's draft performance requirements to eliminate overly restrictive or non-commercial specifications. Refine Acquisition Strategy: Gauge market maturity, delivery lead times, First Article Test (FAT) feasibility, and cost drivers to structure an optimal commercial IDIQ solicitation under streamlined RFO FAR Part 12 procedures. 3. CONTEMPLATED CONTRACT STRUCTURE & SCOPE The Government is contemplating an Indefinite Delivery / Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract structure utilizing FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services) streamlined procedures in conjunction with FAR Part 15 (Contracting by Negotiation): Item Categorization: Modified Commercial Product. The baseline generation system must rely on active production commercial products and components with active commercial part-numbers; prototype or unproven "pre-production" components are not authorized. First Article Test (FAT) Unit: Two (2) initial units subject to qualification, Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory (NRTL) inspection, independent accredited laboratory gas purity verification, and operational verification testing. Production Units: Up to ten (10) production units to be ordered via firm-fixed-price delivery orders across the ordering period based on shipyard operational requirements and subject to availability of funds. Support Services & Spares: Delivery, initial on-site commissioning, operational verification, 24 months of spare consumable parts, standard commercial documentation and manuals, and optional multi-year maintenance service agreements. Contemplated Source Selection Method: Best Value with Tradeoffs in accordance with RFO FAR 12.203 and FAR Part 15, where technical capability, system reliability, delivery schedule, and past performance will be evaluated in relation to total evaluated price. Lowest Price Technically Acceptable in accordance with FAR Part 15, where the lowest price meeting or exceeding the acceptability standards for non-cost factors. 4. SUMMARY OF DRAFT TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS The contemplated system is a ruggedized, portable, special-purpose gaseous nitrogen generation plant packaged for demanding maritime shipyard environments. See attached Draft Statement of Work. 5. REQUESTED INDUSTRY FEEDBACK (RFO FAR PART 12 MARKET RESEARCH) In alignment with RFO FAR Part 12 pre-solicitation policy to minimize barriers to commercial item procurement and identify standard commercial terms, industry partners are requested to provide feedback on the following: Topic A: Commercial Product Availability & Customary Commercial Practice Does your firm currently manufacture, sell, or lease standard commercial nitrogen generation systems that achieve the requested purity? Does your product qualify as a "Commercial Product" or a "Commercial Product with Modifications" under FAR 2.101? What specific modifications would be required to adapt your standard commercial offering to meet the PSNS specifications (e.g., ISO container integration, shipyard color restrictions, specific alarm announcements, acoustic attenuation)? Are these modifications of a type customarily available in the commercial marketplace? What are standard commercial warranty terms, customary commercial maintenance agreements, and commercial service intervals for equipment of this type? Under RFO FAR Part 12, what standard commercial terms and conditions or financing practices should the Government consider incorporating or tailoring? Topic B: Technical Feasibility, Packaging, & Trade-offs Is packaging the complete system within a single ISO container achievable using mature, non-developmental COTS components? If bottle banks or compressors require external placement or a two-container configuration, what are the primary engineering trade-offs (e.g., thermal management, footprint, mobilization time)? What technology type (e.g., multi-stage Pressure Swing Adsorption [PSA], catalytic deoxo purification, hybrid membrane/cryogenic) do you recommend to reliably achieve under fluctuating shipyard demand cycles? Topic C: Operational Profile & Maintenance Cycles Is the requirement for 180 days of continuous operation without scheduled filter/oil/adsorbent servicing commercially standard or viable? If not, what is your standard commercial maintenance schedule? Does the requirement for 7-day autonomous operation present any unforeseen failure modes or safety hazards in an unmanned industrial outdoor yard setting? Topic D: Acquisition Strategy, Lead Times, & Evaluation Factors What is the realistic manufacturing, modification, and FAT lead time for an initial First Article unit following contract award? What lead time is expected for follow-on production delivery orders (e.g., 1�3 units per order)? What are the primary cost and schedule drivers in the draft requirements (e.g., purity verification, acoustic attenuations, marine coating, 180-day continuous run requirement)? Under the contemplated FAR Part 12 / Part 15 Best Value Tradeoff framework, what commercial evaluation factors (e.g., past performance, demonstrated commercial reliability, warranty terms, life-cycle costs) would best enable offerors to propose innovative commercial solutions? 6. title: INVITATION TO SUBMIT AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) AS TO THE AVAILABILITY OF SPACE FOR LEASE IN THE CITY OF COWANSVILLE (QUEBEC)
description: INVITATION TO SUBMIT AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) AS TO THE AVAILABILITY OF SPACE FOR LEASE IN THE CITY OF COWANSVILLE (QUEBEC) FILE NUMBER: 81003487 Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately fifteen (15) years, commencing on or about March 1, 2029; • approximately six hundred nineteen (619) usable square meters (um2) of contiguous office space. • the proposed space must be available approximately twenty-four (24) weeks prior to the above-noted lease commencement date so all space(s) may be prepared for occupancy; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. The proposed space should be contiguous, unobstructed, preferably on the ground floor, although premises located on the second floor could be considered. The Lessee may also consider offices located on a maximum of two contiguous floors including the ground floor and second floor; 2. The proposed building must have a window arrangement and configuration that are acceptable to the lessee; 3. the proposed space should be within an office or commercial building; industrial type buildings and those with industrial space will not be considered; 4. The physical characteristics of the sites and buildings, as well as the use of neighboring land and the surrounding area must be compatible with the intended use; 5. The building where the premises will be located must be fully accessible to everyone, integrating physical, sensory, and cognitive needs; 6. The space must be accessible by public transport; 7. The availability of 15 visitors parking spaces within 500 meters walking distance to be calculated from the building entrance closest to the potential office space using only sidewalks, pedestrian crosswalks and pedestrian paths; ? the proposed space must be located in the city of Cowansville, province of Quebec, and the geographical boundaries exclude agricultural, industrial, and residential areas. Mixed-use real estate zones or project (residential and commercial) could be considered. • on or before the lease commencement date, the proposed space will have to comply with all requirements contained in PSPC’s Standards for Leased Accommodation, a copy of which may be obtained from the contact listed in Section F; Note: PSPC may wish to visit or inspect the proposed space upon reasonable notice and a threat and risk assessment may be undertaken in order to assess potential threats to the security of the proposed space and to the public. Section B: Responses Interested parties are requested to submit their response to this EOI in writing to the following address: Public Services and Procurement Canada Place Bonaventure, South-West Portal 800, de la Gauchetière St West, suite 7300 Montréal (Québec) H5A 1L6 or by email to the contact listed below in Section F. Please indicate File No. 81003487 on all correspondence. Section C: Responses Requested by As this may be the only invitation to submit an Expression of Interest for this potential lease project, owners/mandatories should provide their response by October 16, 2026. Any response received after this date may not be considered. Section D: Information Provided by Interested Parties or Mandatories of Interested Parties Information provided by interested parties or mandatories of interested parties should include the file number, the location and municipal address of the building, current zoning, specific location of space within the building, measured area of space, architectural drawings identifying the proposed space with washrooms, exits and other design elements, and details addressing the criteria listed above in Section A. Mandatories submitting a response to this EOI must provide PSPC with a letter authorizing them to do so. Section E: Security Requirement If this EOI results in a future tender process, the building owners of the proposed spaces will have to hold a valid security clearance at the “Reliability” level, approved and granted by the Canadian Industrial Security Directorate (CISD) of PSPC prior to the beginning of the fit up work. All parties interested in this potential lease project are advised to obtain this security clearance level in advance. Information regarding security clearance can be obtained on the website of the CISD/ PSPC at http://ssi-iss.tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca. Please contact the person listed in Section F to initiate the security clearance process. Section F: Additional Information For more information, please contact Aubray Roy, Senior Leasing Officer by phone at 438-465-0428 or by email to: aubray.roy@tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca. Section G: List of Available Space This EOI is issued in order to invite interested parties to demonstrate their interest in providing the requirements described herein. This information may be included in a list of available space and used for potential future solicitations. Section H: Not a Solicitation Process Note that this is not a tender process, nor a request for proposal, but only an inquiry as to the availability of space to lease. PSPC will not necessarily invite offers, or lease any space, and may not post any future ads related to this request. The information provided through this EOI may be included in a source list of available space and PSPC may issue an invitation to tender for other leasing requirements based on this information, or based on any other information which may come to its attention prior to an issuance of an invitation to tender; or it may invite offers by way of public tender. PSPC reserves the right to proceed with an Invitation to Offer to Lease by inviting only parties deemed to most effectively meet specific operational, security and public safety requirements.

title: JOFOC for Data Analysis for Quality, Safety & Oversight of the ESRD, Transplant, and OPO Programs
description: The contractor will provide detailed data reports about End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) facilities (commonly referred to as dialysis facilities), Transplant Programs, and Organ Procurement Organizations (OPOs) in formats that are useful to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), states, health care providers, and the general public. These reports will include summaries of patient characteristics, facility characteristics, patient outcomes, and facility practice patterns. These reports will include comparative state, network, regional, and national statistics as appropriate. These reports will be used by CMS in overseeing the quality and safety of the ESRD, Transplant and OPO Programs. For the Dialysis Facility Reports (DFRs), the contractor will use data from a variety of sources to create summary reports to be used to provide Federal, state and facility oversight of dialysis facilities. Data from all available sources, including the CMS Central Data Repository (CDR), claims forms, eligibility forms, clinical data sources, facility inventories, death forms, and survey and certification forms will be updated, edited, validated, and utilized by the contractor to create a series of reports that will assist CMS, states, and other entities in monitoring the care provided by ESRD facilities. These reports will be risk-adjusted and facility, state, regional, and corporate-specific for each fiscal year. The reports shall include a rank-ordered Outcomes List of ESRD facilities for each state. The Outcomes Lists will be constructed from a composite of data elements that most validly and reliably identify facilities with potential problems. The contractor will routinely revise the DFRs to ensure they are 1) aligned with the ESRD Survey process, 2) provide development of data sources and data tools to allow state surveyors convenient and timely access to more current dialysis facility quality outcomes, 3) use state surveyor and other DFR user feedback to determine the need for revisions. The contractor will provide guidance on using advanced technologies and incorporate plans to integrate emerging technologies associated with Electronic Health Records (EHRs). The contractor will prepare Transplant Program reports and OPO reports. The data for these reports will be obtained from the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) of the Health Resources and Services Agency (HRSA), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and Multiple Cause of Death (MCOD) databases. This data will be used in the calculation of annual OPO performance measure scores as required by the CMS regulations at 42 CFR �486.318.

title: General Contractor for the Seismic Retrofit Project at the Clemente Ruiz Nazario U.S. Courthouse, San Juan, Puerto Rico
description: THIS IS A SYNOPSIS/PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY. This notice is not a request for offers or proposals. This notice does not represent a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service, Acquisition Project Delivery � Capital Construction Division, intends to solicit for a highly qualified Contractor who can provide Construction Services to perform a Seismic Retrofit at the Clemente Ruiz Nazario U.S. Courthouse (Nazario Courthouse) located at 150 Carlos Chardon Avenue in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Nazario Courthouse will remain fully operational throughout the duration of the Seismic Retrofit. To ensure minimal disruption to Government operations, the work will predominantly be executed after business hours. The selected General Contractor will be required to ensure full compliance with the Government�s requirements for access and security. Additionally, the General Contractor will be required to complete this project in accordance with the construction drawings and specifications that will be issued for this project. Contract Type: The contract type for this procurement will be Firm-Fixed price. The line item schedule will include a lump sum item for the Base and Options. Price: The total magnitude of this project at award is between $40,000,000 and $50,000,000. Selection and Schedule: The General Contractor will be selected through a procurement method developed in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation (Class Deviation RFO-2025-15) and FAR 36 Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-36). The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Evaluation process. During Phase I, prospective firms must submit technical qualifications detailing their experience with comparable efforts and previous records of past-performance. In Phase II, selected General Contractors shall demonstrate their operational strategy and planned subcontracting framework. Evaluation of Phase II technical submissions will be conducted in full before the Government reviews the price proposal. GSA anticipates award of a contract for these services in August 2027. The period of performance for the proposed contract will be for approximately forty six (46) months upon issuance of notice to proceed. NAICS: This procurement will be conducted under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 236220--Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Small Business size standard is an average annual sales and receipts for the past three (3) years that are equal to or less than $45,000,000. Solicitation Information: GSA anticipates issuing the Solicitation on or about October 19, 2026, with receipt of Phase I proposals due at a minimum of forty-five (45) calendar days later. All information, amendments and questions concerning this solicitation will be electronically posted to the Government-wide Point of Entry at www.SAM.gov. No telephone requests will be accepted and no paper copies will be mailed to prospective offerors. A bid guarantee (bid bond) will be required at twenty (20) percent of the bid price or $3 million, whichever is less, at the time of Phase II proposal submission. Upon contract award, both the Performance and Payment bonds will be required at 100% of the total contract value. Any firms unable to meet the bond requirements will be ineligible for a contract award. All offerors are required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (www.SAM.gov) at the time of offer submission, and shall continue to be registered until time of award, during performance and through final payment of the contract. In addition, in order for contractors to have access to Federal space, the contractor will be required to adhere to the Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12), Directive Clearance Process, in accordance with FAR 52.204-9 - Personal Identity Verification of Contractor Personnel (JAN 2011) as well as other security clearances that may be required.

description: CBP has a requirement to continue Saleforce CoI Professional Services through Steampunk Inc. title: Y1DA--561A4-23-101 Replace Hot Water Heaters
description: Presolicitation Notice Presolicitation Notice Page 4 of 4 Presolicitation Notice *=Required Field Presolicitation Notice Page 1 of 4 This notice is for Solicitation Number 36C24226B0052, Project Number 561A4-23-101 Replace Multiple Building s Water Heaters at the VA Health Care System, Lyons Campus, 151 Knollcroft Rd., Lyons, NJ 07939-5001. This shall be a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Set-Aside. As a result, all SDVOSB's may submit a bid, which will be considered by the agency. This project is classified under NAICS Code 238220 and has a size standard of $19 Million. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. Scope of Work: The scope of work shall generally consist of, but not limited to the following: The project involves upgrading the Hot Water Heater system (specifically Buildings 3, 7, 53, 54, and 143 and their associated mechanical and utility spaces). The existing domestic hot water heating systems at the Lyons VA Medical Center consist of aging tank type and semi-instantaneous water heaters and associated recirculation pumps that are inefficient, and beyond their intended service life. These units serve critical patient care, residential, and support areas and must be upgraded to meet current VA design standards, energy efficiency requirements, and plumbing and electrical codes while maintaining continuous hot water service to the occupied facility. The water heaters shall be replaced sequentially so that only one unit is taken out of service at a given time, and the others remain in full operation. This approach will ensure continuous domestic hot water service to the building throughout construction, with at least one operational hot water heater. Replacing these units will significantly reduce maintenance time, improve system control and enhance the distribution of hot water across rooms, floors, and departments. The contractor shall completely prepare site for building operations, including demolishing selected existing water heaters, recirculation pumps, and associated steam, condensate, and domestic water piping and furnish and install new semi-instantaneous steam to hot water heaters, recirculation pumps, condensate receiver/pump, piping, insulation, electrical feeders, disconnects, and controls as indicated in the 100% construction documents. Work also includes startup, testing, balancing, commissioning and training the VA plumbing staff on the new equipment. The contractor shall also furnish all labor, materials, tool, and supervision necessary to perform work for VA Project 561A4-23-101 Replace Multiple Building s Water Heaters, in accordance with AE drawings and specifications. Project Completion: 180 Calendar Days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). All other details and information shall be contained in the solicitation which shall be posted on www.sam.gov. The solicitation will be released on or about July 20, 2026. The response submittal address, date and time will be included in the solicitation. This project requires bonding and all responses/submissions to the solicitation to be posted later shall be emailed. No hand-carried bids will be accepted. All prospective bidders must be currently registered in www.sam.gov , and be registered and verified as a Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) in https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ at the time of offer submission and before award of this procurement. End of Description.

description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awarded Contract No. 75D30126P21489 to the Texas Department of State Health Services for the Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System � Texas. title: Contingency Transportation Services BPA
description: This Notice is prepared in accordance with RFO 5.1 and RFO 12.201-1(c)(2). THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS. The Government intends to solicit this requirement directly from qualified suppliers in accordance with RFO 12.201-1(c)(2) for a firm-fixed-price contract as outlined in the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). This Notice is issued solely for informational and market research planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, bid guarantee, or promise of contract award. The Government reserves the right to cancel or amend this procurement at any time. The Government is not responsible for, nor will it reimburse, any costs incurred by interested vendors or commercial entities in the preparation, compilation, or submission of responses to this Pre-Solicitation Notice. All participation is strictly voluntary and at the vendor's sole expense. REQUIREMENT OVERVIEW & SCOPE OF WORK The 356th Expeditionary Theater Support Group (ETSG) requires reliable, responsive, and secure commercial line haul and heavy equipment transport services across various military installations and port facilities on the island of Guam. Key performance parameters include: Service Scope: Safe transport, line haul, and handling of tactical/non-tactical vehicles, tracked heavy machinery (e.g., bulldozers, excavators), associated gear, and general freight cargo. Key Operational Locations: Performance involves transportation services to, from, and between Andersen Air Force Base (AAFB), Naval Station (NAVSTA) Guam Port Operations (Apra Harbor), Jose D. Leon Guerrero Commercial Port (Piti), Antonio B. Won Pat International Airport (GUM), and designated commercial or military maintenance yards. Notice and Scheduling: Standard transport requirements will be scheduled with a minimum of ninety-six (96) hours advanced notice. Emergency transport requests with less than 96 hours notice must be mutually agreed upon by the Contractor and the Government. Equipment and Cargo Securement: 100% compliance with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) and Department of Transportation (DOT) standards is required. buyer: European Commission, FPI - Service for Foreign Policy Instruments
title: Canada – Public relations services – Policy Dialogue and Public Diplomacy Facility for Canada
description: The purpose of this procurement is to procure services that strengthen and deepen EU–Canada relations on key priority themes of shared strategic interest, while advancing EU interests and values in Canada through targeted policy dialogue and public diplomacy. The contract will support the implementation of commitments under the EU–Canada Strategic Partnership Agreement (SPA), the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), and, where relevant, other bilateral frameworks including the EU–Canada Green Alliance and the EU–Canada Security and Defence Partnership. The procured services shall comprise two complementary components: Policy Dialogue Support — facilitation of structured policy dialogues across a wide range of areas through concrete activities linked to existing and emerging dialogue mechanisms, including joint committees and working groups involving the EU Delegation and relevant EU services. Public Diplomacy Actions — Design and delivery of public diplomacy initiatives aimed at increasing understanding of EU policies and priorities among Canadian audiences, demonstrating the tangible benefits of the EU–Canada partnership, and strengthening engagement with key Canadian stakeholders beyond government — including media, academia, civil society, youth, and opinion leaders. The services shall deliver measurable policy outcomes, consolidate trusted stakeholder networks, and amplify EU positions across Canada. Through the combined effect of policy dialogue and public diplomacy, the procurement aims to enhance the visibility and credibility of the EU in Canada and contribute to closer alignment between EU and Canadian policy positions and approaches, including in multilateral fora, on major foreign policy priorities.

title: GOCO Industry Day
description: Executive Summary The current operating strategy for Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) Army ammunition plants requires reassessment to ensure the Organic Industrial Base can meet future requirements for safety, responsiveness, capacity, modernization, supply-chain resilience, and affordable lifecycle performance. Traditional GOCO competition and contract approaches may not consistently create the incentives, flexibility, or accountability necessary to operate Government-owned facilities as modern and competitive manufacturing enterprises. In particular, existing approaches may overemphasize Government-directed workload and reimbursed facility operations rather than operator responsibility for productive utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce development, workload capture, and operational performance. The Government is seeking industry input on a commercially disciplined GOCO operating model that preserves Government mission priorities while providing the operating contractor meaningful responsibility and flexibility to manage the facility as a competitive manufacturing enterprise. Under such a model, the contractor would be expected to sustain, modernize, maintain, and improve the facility through efficient operations, productive utilization, pursuit of approved workload, and sound business practices. The Government seeks to identify contracting, workload, risk-allocation, facility-use, oversight, intellectual-property, and performance-management constructs that will enable this model while preserving appropriate Government accountability, safety, security, and access to required production capacity. Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE AS&A) is assessing the future GOCO operating strategy before proceeding with future GOCO competitions. Purpose Army Contracting Command � Rock Island, on behalf of PAE AS&A, intends to host an Industry Day in November 2026 focused on transforming the operating strategy for GOCO Army ammunition plants. Specific Industry Day details will be provided separately; registration is not currently required. This Request for Information (RFI), together with the subsequent Industry Day, will help the Government understand feasible business and operating models for future GOCO facilities. The Government will use industry feedback to inform discussion of alternative approaches to facility operations, modernization, workload management, contract structure, and oversight. Objective The Government�s objective is to establish a commercially disciplined operating model for GOCO Army ammunition plants that improves responsiveness to Warfighter requirements while sustaining long-term plant viability, modernization, competitiveness, and accountability. The desired model would provide the operating contractor with appropriate flexibility and meaningful responsibility to manage facility utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce, supply chain, and approved workload. The Government seeks input on the risk-allocation mechanisms, workload authorities, facility-use structures, performance measures, and oversight approaches necessary to support this model while preserving Government mission priorities. The desired end state is a modern, flexible production enterprise capable of efficiently increasing, reducing, pausing, restarting, changing over, and surging production in response to Warfighter need without disproportionate impacts to cost, schedule, quality, workforce readiness, safety, or production capability. The Government is particularly interested in performance measures that demonstrate: Safe and reliable operations; Schedule reliability and order-to-delivery responsiveness; Plant availability and production throughput; Rapid changeover, shutdown, restart, and surge capability; Flexible, modular, dual-use, and/or automated manufacturing capacity; Effective maintenance, workforce, and supply-chain management; Competitive lifecycle cost and productive utilization; Modernization outcomes that improve operating performance; and Appropriate transparency and accountability without unnecessary Government direction of day-to-day operations. Areas of Consideration The Government developed the attached questionnaire based on the following interconnected areas of consideration. Respondents are requested to complete the associated questionnaire and provide practical recommendations, examples, and lessons learned from relevant commercial, defense-industrial, or other manufacturing environments. The Government is particularly interested in responses that: Describe a complete and coherent commercial operating model rather than isolated contractual changes; Identify recommended Government and contractor responsibilities; Explain the proposed allocation of risk and opportunity; Identify measurable outcomes and recommended key performance indicators; Describe the conditions necessary to modernize facilities and maintain flexible production capacity; Address how the model would operate during high-demand, low-demand, shutdown, restart, and surge conditions; Identify legal, regulatory, technical, security, safety, qualification, or business constraints requiring further Government consideration; and Contain data that supports its recommended solutions. 1. Commercial Operating Model and Risk Allocation The Government seeks input on operating models in which the contractor manages a Government-owned facility with commercial discipline while meeting Government mission priorities. Topics may include: Operator responsibilities, decision rights, and accountability; Allocation of demand, utilization, revenue, operating-cost, maintenance, modernization, obsolescence, and performance risk; Contractor responsibility for productive utilization and continuous improvement; Mechanisms that encourage modernization as an operating outcome rather than a discrete facility-improvement project; Gain-sharing, profit-sharing, retained earnings, or reinvestment approaches; Treatment of contractor-funded improvements at contract transition; and Protection of Government interests while maintaining meaningful contractor performance and market risk. 2. Demand, Capacity, and Workload Management The Government seeks input on how Government requirements and approved non-Government workload can be integrated to improve plant utilization, responsiveness, and long-term viability. Topics may include: Government demand forecasting and demand-signal quality; Government mission-priority requirements; Capacity reservation, surge, turn-down, shutdown, restart, and reconstitution; Minimum Government commitments, if necessary, and the appropriate purpose and scope of such commitments; Integration of Government, commercial, Foreign Military Sales, and other approved workload; Multi-year procurement and workload-planning approaches; Workforce retention and readiness during periods of variable demand; and Mechanisms for balancing Government access to capacity with contractor responsibility for utilization. 3. Modern, Flexible, and Resilient Production The Government seeks concepts for modernizing GOCO production capability to improve agility, resilience, and efficient response to changing demand. Topics may include: Flexible, modular, dual-use, and automated production lines; Rapid product changeover and qualification; Planned shutdown, restart, and surge capability; Automation, robotics, digital manufacturing, digital twins, and predictive maintenance; Equipment replacement, facility renewal, and obsolescence management; Workforce cross-training and critical-skill retention; Supply-chain resilience and access to existing U.S. industrial capacity; and Technical, regulatory, contractual, qualification, or facility barriers that limit modernization and flexibility. 4.
