title: CFA-686 Carbon-based Fuels Capability - CO2 Storage Vessel
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to support the design, fabrication, testing, and inspection of a pressure vessel for the Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability. PROCESS BEA is seeking qualified firms to compete for the design/build contract in support of the CFA-686 CO2 Storage Vessel (V-738). As determined by BEA, responders to this EOI may receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) that will require detailed technical and price proposals be provided for evaluation and ranking under a source selection process. Interested firms are advised that RFP release and the source selection/award decision timeline will be communicated following review of submitted EOIs. The contract award type will be firm?fixed price. The total anticipated duration for completion of all work is 28 weeks ARO, and the estimated sequential schedule is as follows: ASME Code design and analysis (3 weeks), shop fabrication drawings (4 weeks), WPS/PQR submittal and approval (3 weeks), complete shop fabrication including cleaning (25 weeks), install heating elements and insulate vessel (26 weeks), ship vessel to INL (27 weeks), and submission of the final Code Data Report, as?built drawings, and all other deliverables (28 weeks). PROJECT DESCRIPTION The vessel will be designed, fabricated, inspected, and delivered for the INL Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability (CFA-686). The vessel, designated V-738, is a 200 cubic foot ASME BPVC Section VIII, Division 1 code "U" stamped pressure vessel for gaseous CO2 service, with a design pressure of 1,800 psig and a design temperature range of -40�F to 500�F. The vessel is a horizontal configuration with two saddle supports spaced 16 feet apart, a 36-inch inner diameter, minimum 2-inch shell thickness, minimum 1-inch hemispherical head thickness, and an overall shell length of 26 feet 3-1/2 inches. The vessel includes seven nozzles (inlet, outlet, five inspection ports, a low point drain, a pressure relief nozzle, and two instrumentation ports), nine band heating elements (3.6 kW total) to maintain the vessel above 150�F, and Foamglas (or equivalent) insulation with protective aluminum sheathing. The vessel will be installed outdoors at INL in a high desert environment, with an altitude of 4,900 ft, ambient temperatures ranging from -40�F to 100�F, and exposure to wind, blowing sand, dust, snow, and frost. The vessel must be designed for static, seismic, and wind loading in accordance with IBC 2024, ASCE 7-10, and ACI 318-19, and fabricated from 304/304L stainless steel pressure boundary materials. Specific fabrication drawings, foundation details, and design calculations will be provided to qualified offerors as part of the RFP process. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest to Chase Egbert (chase.egbert@inl.gov) by close-of-business on 10/16/2026. Included must be sufficient written information confirming the responder's qualifications addressing each of the following criteria: Experience in ASME BPVC Section VIII, Division 1 pressure vessel design and fabrication, including possession of a current "U" stamp certificate for both design and fabrication. Experience with stainless steel pressure vessel welding, including full penetration butt welds, 100% radiography, and carbide precipitation control during welding. Capability to meet the design/build schedule outlined above. Capability to fabricate the vessel in the required configuration, including nozzle arrangement, saddle supports, band heating elements, and insulation system. Proper identification and execution plan for inspection, examination, and testing, including hydrostatic testing, positive material identification, liquid penetrant testing, and radiography or phased array ultrasonic testing. Agreement to maintain a written Quality Control System consistent with ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1, Mandatory Appendix 10. Compliance with ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1, Mandatory Appendix 47 requirements for pressure vessel design. Availability of a qualified and experienced project manager and Quality Control Manager to oversee the work. Note that responses must be no more than 5 pages in length. Only potentially qualified offerors, as determined by BEA, will receive the RFP for the project. Interested individuals are advised that the selection decision is anticipated in November 2026. If you have questions, need additional information, or need to speak with a BEA Point of Contact, please contact the following via email: Project Manager - Ben Bryson - Benjamin.Bryson@inl.gov Project Engineer - Chris Dudley- Christopher.Dudley@inl.gov Technical questions must be submitted in writing via email.

title: CFA-686 Carbon-based Fuels Capability CO2 Compressor Design/Build
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to support the design, fabrication, testing, and delivery of a CO2 compressor for the Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability. PROCESS BEA is seeking qualified firms to compete for the design/build contract in support of the CFA-686 CO2 Compressor. As determined by BEA, responders to this EOI may receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) that will require detailed technical and price proposals be provided for evaluation and ranking under a source selection process. Interested firms are advised that RFP release and the source selection/award decision timeline will be communicated following review of submitted EOIs. The contract award type will be firm-fixed price. Per the proposed project schedule, all durations are After Receipt of Order (ARO): Engineering Documentation Report (3 weeks), shop fabrication drawings (4 weeks), complete shop fabrication (40 weeks), and compressor arrival at INL (3 weeks). PROJECT DESCRIPTION The compressor will be designed, fabricated, tested, and delivered for the INL Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability (CFA-686). The compressor will be used to compress CO2 from a combustor unit into a storage vessel that will supply gas to downstream users, and will be housed in a protected shipping container. The compressor shall be oil-free, liquid-cooled, fixed speed, and electric motor driven. Inlet conditions are 50-100�F at 0.14-2 psig; outlet conditions are 1,400 psig, 66.1 scfm, and 150�F, with the unit operating on a nearly continuous basis. The compressor and all components must fit within a high cube shipping container with interior dimensions of 19'6" long x 7'9" wide x 8'10" high, and must be mounted on a structural frame designed and fabricated in accordance with the American Institute of Steel Construction (AISC), with welding per AWS D1.1. Any pressure vessels used in fabrication of the compressor must be designed and fabricated in accordance with ASME Section VIII, Division 1, and stamped and registered with the National Board. The compressor must withstand a CO2 gas stream composition of approximately 99% CO2 with trace nitrogen, oxygen, water vapor, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, sulfur oxides, hydrocarbons, hydrogen sulfide, and hydrogen chloride. The unit will be installed at INL at an altitude of approximately 4,938 ft, with a shipping container temperature range of 41�F to 104�F and humidity from 0 to 100%. The compressor package must include a control panel with instrumentation and alarms for conditions such as low discharge pressure and motor failure, a data history logging function, an emergency shutoff switch, and UL-508A listed control panels. The unit must be provided with inter-coolers or after-coolers to maintain outlet temperature at or below 150�F, and a stainless steel drip pan sized to contain at least 1.5 times the volume of any fluids contained in the compressor. Specific fabrication drawings, nozzle location diagrams, and design details will be provided to qualified offerors as part of the RFP process. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest to Chase Egbert (chase.egbert@inl.gov) by close-of-business on 10/16/2026. Included must be sufficient written information confirming the responder's qualifications addressing each of the following criteria: Experience in design and fabrication of oil-free, liquid-cooled CO2 or industrial gas compressor packages. Experience with ASME Section VIII, Division 1 pressure vessel design where applicable to compressor components, and structural fabrication in accordance with AISC and AWS D1.1. Capability to meet the design/build schedule outlined above. Capability to package the compressor, motor, controls, and all interconnecting piping and instrumentation within the required shipping container footprint. Proper identification and execution plan for inspection, examination, and testing, including non-destructive examination of castings and welds, operational testing, and a 10-hour continuous reliability test. Agreement to maintain a written Quality Assurance Plan based on a national consensus code such as ANSI/ASME ISO-9000. Capability to provide Operations & Maintenance documentation, a Recommended Spare Parts List, and field support for startup and commissioning. Note that responses must be no more than 5 pages in length. Only potentially qualified offerors, as determined by BEA, will receive the RFP for the project. Interested individuals are advised that the selection decision is anticipated in November 2026. If you have questions, need additional information, or need to speak with a BEA Point of Contact, please contact the following via email: Project Manager - Ben Bryson - Benjamin.Bryson@inl.gov Project Engineer - Chris Dudley - Christopher.Dudley@inl.gov Technical questions must be submitted in writing via email.

title: CFA-686 Carbon-based Fuels Capability - CO2 Storage Vessel
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to support the design, fabrication, testing, and inspection of a pressure vessel for the Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability. PROCESS BEA is seeking qualified firms to compete for the design/build contract in support of the CFA-686 CO2 Storage Vessel (V-738). As determined by BEA, responders to this EOI may receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) that will require detailed technical and price proposals be provided for evaluation and ranking under a source selection process. Interested firms are advised that RFP release and the source selection/award decision timeline will be communicated following review of submitted EOIs. The contract award type will be firm-fixed price. Per the project schedule, all durations are After Receipt of Order (ARO): ASME Code design and analysis (3 weeks), shop fabrication drawings (4 weeks), WPS/PQR submittal and approval (3 weeks), complete shop fabrication including cleaning (25 weeks), install heating elements and insulate vessel (26 weeks), ship vessel to INL (27 weeks), and submission of the final Code Data Report, as-built drawings, and all other deliverables (28 weeks). PROJECT DESCRIPTION The vessel will be designed, fabricated, inspected, and delivered for the INL Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability (CFA-686). The vessel, designated V-738, is a 200 cubic foot ASME BPVC Section VIII, Division 1 code "U" stamped pressure vessel for gaseous CO2 service, with a design pressure of 1,800 psig and a design temperature range of -40�F to 500�F. The vessel is a horizontal configuration with two saddle supports spaced 16 feet apart, a 36-inch inner diameter, minimum 2-inch shell thickness, minimum 1-inch hemispherical head thickness, and an overall shell length of 26 feet 3-1/2 inches. The vessel includes seven nozzles (inlet, outlet, five inspection ports, a low point drain, a pressure relief nozzle, and two instrumentation ports), nine band heating elements (3.6 kW total) to maintain the vessel above 150�F, and Foamglas (or equivalent) insulation with protective aluminum sheathing. The vessel will be installed outdoors at INL in a high desert environment, with an altitude of 4,900 ft, ambient temperatures ranging from -40�F to 100�F, and exposure to wind, blowing sand, dust, snow, and frost. The vessel must be designed for static, seismic, and wind loading in accordance with IBC 2024, ASCE 7-10, and ACI 318-19, and fabricated from 304/304L stainless steel pressure boundary materials. Specific fabrication drawings, foundation details, and design calculations will be provided to qualified offerors as part of the RFP process. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest to Chase Egbert (chase.egbert@inl.gov) by close-of-business on 10/16/2026. Included must be sufficient written information confirming the responder's qualifications addressing each of the following criteria: Experience in ASME BPVC Section VIII, Division 1 pressure vessel design and fabrication, including possession of a current "U" stamp certificate for both design and fabrication. Experience with stainless steel pressure vessel welding, including full penetration butt welds, 100% radiography, and carbide precipitation control during welding. Capability to meet the design/build schedule outlined above. Capability to fabricate the vessel in the required configuration, including nozzle arrangement, saddle supports, band heating elements, and insulation system. Proper identification and execution plan for inspection, examination, and testing, including hydrostatic testing, positive material identification, liquid penetrant testing, and radiography or phased array ultrasonic testing. Agreement to maintain a written Quality Control System consistent with ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1, Mandatory Appendix 10. Compliance with ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1, Mandatory Appendix 47 requirements for pressure vessel design. Availability of a qualified and experienced project manager and Quality Control Manager to oversee the work. Note that responses must be no more than 5 pages in length. Only potentially qualified offerors, as determined by BEA, will receive the RFP for the project. Interested individuals are advised that the selection decision is anticipated in November 2026. If you have questions, need additional information, or need to speak with a BEA Point of Contact, please contact the following via email: Project Manager - Ben Bryson - Benjamin.Bryson@inl.gov Project Engineer - Chris Dudley- Christopher.Dudley@inl.gov Technical questions must be submitted in writing via email.

Ansökan om erforderliga tillstånd för uppförande av objektet, innefattande bygglov och startbesked enligt PBL, samt medverkan i tekniskt samråd, kontroll och slutsamråd intill dess att slutbesked erhållits. 4. Besiktning och övriga moment som erfordras för att objektet ska kunna tas i bruk för avsett ändamål. Fullständiga förutsättningar framgår i upphandlingsdokumenten.

title: Finland – Health and social work services – Holter-palveluiden hankinta
description: Kainuun hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia Holter -palveluista Kainuun keskussairaalaan sisätaudeille ja lastentaudeille sekä Suomussalmen, Kuhmon, Puolangan ja Sotkamon terveysasemille erikoissairaanhoidon toimintana. Arvioitu sopimuskausi on 1.3.2027- 28.2.2029. Sopimuskausi alkaa, kun molemmat sopijapuolet ovat allekirjoittaneet sopimuksen ja kestää kaksi (2) vuotta. Lisäksi tilaaja varaa option 1 + 1 vuodelle. Palveluun sisältyvät laitteisto, automaattinen tiedonsiirto, analysointi ja kardiologian lausunto. Holter-rekisteröintilaitteista vastaa palveluntuottaja. Laitteen luovuttaa asiakkaalle hoitaja joko Kainuun keskussairaalan sisätautien poliklinikalta tai Suomussalmen, Kuhmon, Puolangan ja Sotkamon terveyskeskuksista. Asiakas palauttaa laitteen hoitohenkilökunnalle, joka purkaa rekisteröinnin ja esitiedot palveluntuottajan sähköiseen järjestelmään/palveluun. Lausunto tulee olla sähköisessä muodossa ja potilaan oirepäiväkirja tulee olla suoraan analyysipalveluun liitettävä. Rekisteröinnin tulee tapahtua ilman henkilötietoja. Tallenteiden purkaminen ei vaadi käyttäjältä erillistä ohjelmistoa tallenteiden käsittelyyn vaan raakatallenteet lähetetään palveluntuottajalle rekisteröintijärjestelmän sivuston kautta. Hoitava lääkäri saa selkeän lausunnon jatkosuosituksineen pdf-tiedostona ja lausunto tulee olla liitettävissä potilaan tietoihin järjestelmään: Commitwebb; kuva-arkisto Sectra IDS7:ään. Palvelulle asetetut vaatimukset esitetty tarjouspyynnön Muut ehdot ja Hankinnan kohteen kriteerit kohdissa. Holter-laitteiden tarve Kainuun hyvinvointialueelle on kaiken kaikkiaan 11 laitetta (sisältäen Kainuun keskussairaalan, jokaisen Kainuun alueen terveyskeskuksen ja lasten laitteiden tarpeet).

title: Justification for Other Than Full and Open - Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System � California
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awarded Contract No. 75D30126P21605 to the California Department of Public Health for the Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System � California. The contract was awarded on a sole-source basis pursuant to RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The requirement is for the identification and provision of California vital records necessary to support CDC's Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System. The California Department of Public Health is the sole legal custodian and authoritative source of the required California vital records. Market research confirmed that the required records are maintained exclusively by the State of California and are not available from other sources in the required format. The contract includes a 12-month Base Period and four 12-month Option Periods. The Base Period value is $10,074.43, and the total potential contract value, is $49,012.15. In accordance with RFO Part 6, the approved Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC) is being made publicly available with this notice. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. The contract has already been awarded, and the Government is not soliciting or accepting proposals in response to this notice. This notice is being published solely to provide public notice of the award and the associated Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC).

title: Bulgaria – Miscellaneous evaluation or testing instruments – Доставка на оборудване и консумативи за лаборатория „Молекулярна биология“ по 5 обособени позиции
description: Предмет на настоящата обществена поръчка е доставка на специализирано лабораторно оборудване и консумативи за молекулярно-биологичен анализ, което да позволи на високо научно ниво да се дефинира влиянието на променливи фактори, обусловени от климатичните изменения, върху генетичния отговор на лозята, включително експресията на гени, свързани с устойчивост към биотичен и абиотичен стрес, както и ранно откриване на патогени (вируси, бактерии, фитоплазми и гъби) по лозата. Поръчката включва следните обособени позиции: Обособена позиция №1: „Доставка на консумативи за PCR и Real time PCR за текуща лабораторна работа“; Обособена позиция №2: „Доставка на ламинарни боксове (микробиологичен клас II А2 и за PCR) и лабораторна камина“; Обособена позиция № 3: „Доставка на общолабораторно оборудване“; Обособена позиция № 4: „Доставка на Автоклав“; Обособена позиция № 5: “Доставка на олигонуклеотиди (PCR праймери)”. ​​​​Дейността се финансира като част от проект „Адаптиране на лозарството към изменението на климата чрез прилагане на екосистемни мерки за поддържане на икономическата жизнеспособност (VitiClimRoBg–Hard ROBG00370)“, по Програма Interreg VI-A Румъния-България, специфична цел: 2.4 — Насърчаване на адаптирането към изменението на климата, предотвратяването на риска от бедствия и устойчивостта, като се вземат предвид екосистемни подходи. Специализираното оборудване, обект на настоящата обществена поръчка, е в интеграция с предходно заявени компоненти по проекта, за да се постигне интегриран комплексен подход, пряко обвързан с адаптацията към климатичните изменения. Целта е допълване на теренни и физикохимични данни с молекулярно-генетичен анализ, предоставящ прецизни, възпроизводими и научно обосновани резултати, които да очертаят връзката на климатичните изменения с генетичните механизми на адаптация на лозята, генерирайки последователно прилагане на устойчиви практики за „борба“ с климатичния отпечатък и установяване на икономическа жизнеспособност.
